# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

Contents of file README.md: 1 | ﻿# MRI Vision Core — V0.4 2 | 3 | Python/OpenCV MRI exploration with a Streamlit UI, Stanford MRNet label integration, and a lightweight CPU predictive baseline. 4 | 5 | Research and educational prototype. Not for medical diagnosis or clinical decision-making. 6 | 7 | > **Model-safety notice.** The Streamlit app can display experimental CNN probabilities for RSNA knee MRI studies. The only checkpoint that has been produced is a **smoke-test checkpoint**: it was trained for a few seconds on 3 training studies solely to validate the end-to-end software pipeline. Its predictions are **not a measure of clinical performance**, are not clinically meaningful, and are not a diagnosis. No sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, or clinical validation exists for any RSNA model in this repository. 8 | 9 | See the [Visual walkthrough](#visual-walkthrough) for screenshots of the current application. 10 | 11 | ## Milestones 12 | 13 | - **V0.1 completed:** Standard image loading, OpenCV preprocessing, threshold segmentation, overlays, and image features. 14 | - **V0.2 completed:** DICOM/NIfTI loading, `MRIVolume`, slice navigation, and MRI-aware preprocessing. 15 | - **V0.3 completed:** Stanford MRNet `.npy` loading, local plane/exam discovery, and UI exploration. The verified V0.3 baseline was **21 passing tests**, including a local MRNet check. 16 | - **V0.4 completed:** Stanford MRNet label integration, validated examination manifests, and a first predictive baseline for abnormality, ACL tear, and meniscal tear. ROI selection is not this milestone. 17 | 18 | ## Architecture 19 | 20 | The Streamlit application (`app.py`) uses the existing slice-processing core: 21 | 22 | `loader.py` / `dataset_discovery.py` → `mri_volume.py` → `preprocessing.py` → `segmentation.py` → `features.py` / `visualization.py`, orchestrated by `pipeline.py`. 23 | 24 | Supported inputs include DICOM, NIfTI, PNG/JPG, and MRNet NumPy volumes. The UI provides plane/exam selection, slice navigation, technical metadata, Otsu/adaptive masks, and overlays. The MRNet handcrafted-feature baseline runs through a separate CLI, while the experimental RSNA CNN inference path is integrated into the Streamlit app (see [Current application architecture](#current-application-architecture-rsna-workflow) below): 25 | 26 | | Module | Responsibility | 27 | |---|---| 28 | | `mri_core/labels.py` | Strict label parsing, explicit anomaly recovery, task alignment, split validation | 29 | | `mri_core/manifest.py` | ID-based joins, plane availability, separate external image paths, missing/ambiguous image checks | 30 | | `mri_core/baseline_features.py` | Read-only sampled-slice handcrafted features | 31 | | `mri_core/baseline.py` | Train-only fitting, held-out metrics, reproducible CLI and reports | 32 | 33 | ### Current application architecture (RSNA workflow) 34 | 35 | The Streamlit app's **Explore RSNA Studies** mode runs two independent paths from the same DICOM volume and presents them side by side. The **deterministic path** (blue) uses classical image processing with no learned weights and produces the image-quality status. The **experimental path** (orange) is an optional CNN that outputs 12 probabilities. The two paths only meet in the `DecisionReport` container, which stores them in separate fields. 36 | 37 | ```mermaid 38 | flowchart TD 39 | A["RSNA DICOM Study
local files, read-only"] --> B["Study + Plane Selection
Streamlit sidebar"] 40 | B --> C["Multi-slice MRI Volume
ordered DICOM series"] 41 | 42 | subgraph DET["DETERMINISTIC PATH - image processing and quality, no learned weights"] 43 | D["MRI-aware Preprocessing
selected slice"] --> E["Segmentation
Otsu or adaptive threshold + morphology"] 44 | E --> F["Overlay"] 45 | E --> G["Deterministic Image Features
intensity stats, foreground, contours"] 46 | G --> H["Quality Assessment
Quality Status: OK / REVIEW / INVALID"] 47 | end 48 | 49 | subgraph EXP["EXPERIMENTAL PATH - optional CNN, opt-in smoke checkpoint only"] 50 | I["3-Plane Model Input
Axial / Coronal / Sagittal
up to 9 sampled slices per plane, 128x128"] --> J["RSNAKneeCNN"] 51 | J --> K["12 logits"] 52 | K --> L["Sigmoid probabilities
12 ordered study-level targets"] 53 | end 54 | 55 | C --> D 56 | C --> I 57 | H --> M["DecisionReport
quality_status and model_predictions
are separate fields"] 58 | L --> M 59 | M --> N["Streamlit UI
quality report and experimental probabilities shown together"] 60 | P["Research and educational prototype.
Not for medical diagnosis or clinical decision-making."] 61 | N --- P 62 | 63 | classDef det fill:#bfdcff,stroke:#1f4e79,color:#000000 64 | classDef exp fill:#ffd9a0,stroke:#9c5a00,color:#000000 65 | classDef shared fill:#c9ecc4,stroke:#2e6b2a,color:#000000 66 | classDef warn fill:#ffc9c9,stroke:#a10000,color:#000000 67 | class D,E,F,G,H det 68 | class I,J,K,L exp 69 | class A,B,C,M,N shared 70 | class P warn 71 | style DET fill:#eef6ff,stroke:#1f4e79,color:#000000 72 | style EXP fill:#fff4e2,stroke:#9c5a00,color:#000000 73 | ``` 74 | 75 | What the diagram means in the current implementation: 76 | 77 | - **The quality path never sees the model.** Quality Status is computed only from the processed image, its measurements, and volume-level checks. CNN probabilities are validated (finite, within 0-1) and stored next to the status, but they cannot change it. 78 | - **The model path does not use the 2D preprocessing or segmentation.** Model input is built directly from the DICOM series by the training dataset class, which applies its own per-slice normalization (1st/99th percentile clip) and bilinear resize. 79 | - **Inference is study-level.** All three planes are used regardless of which plane is being viewed; each plane contributes one series (fluid-sensitive preferred, lowest `SeriesInstanceUID` as the tie-break). Up to 9 slices per plane are sampled at evenly spaced positions; shorter series use all their slices. 80 | - **The model produces 12 ordered study-level binary targets** as raw logits, converted to probabilities with one sigmoid each: `ACL`, `MCL`, `Medial Meniscus`, `Lateral Meniscus`, `Medial OA`, `Lateral OA`, `PF OA`, `Effusion`, `Synovitis`, `Baker's`, `Contusion`, `Fracture`. 81 | - **Streamlit presents both paths together**, and the CNN path degrades gracefully: with no checkpoint, an incomplete study, or an incompatible checkpoint, the app shows a non-fatal message and still renders the full quality report. 82 | 83 | | Stage | Implementation | 84 | |---|---| 85 | | Study and plane discovery (read-only, tolerant of partial downloads) | `mri_core/rsna_integration.py` | 86 | | DICOM series to ordered volume | `mri_core/dicom_series.py`, `mri_core/mri_volume.py`, `load_series_volume` / `select_series` in `mri_core/rsna_knee_dataset.py` | 87 | | Preprocessing, segmentation, overlay, features | `mri_core/preprocessing.py`, `segmentation.py`, `visualization.py`, `features.py`, orchestrated by `pipeline.py` | 88 | | Deterministic quality assessment and report container | `mri_core/decision.py` (`DecisionReport`, `generate_decision_report`) | 89 | | Three-plane model input | `RSNAKneeDicomDataset` in `mri_core/rsna_knee_train.py` | 90 | | Model | `RSNAKneeCNN` in `mri_core/rsna_knee_model.py` (shared encoder from `mri_core/cnn_model.py`, 3 planes, 12 outputs, 102,012 parameters) | 91 | | Single-study inference | `run_inference` in `mri_core/rsna_knee_inference.py` (CPU, `model.eval()`, `torch.inference_mode()`, validated checkpoint) | 92 | | UI | `app.py` | 93 | 94 | **Deterministic quality assessment.** `generate_decision_report` evaluates the displayed slice after preprocessing and segmentation, plus volume-level facts. The status describes image and pipeline quality only and is never a clinical statement: 95 | 96 | | Status | Meaning | 97 | |---|---| 98 | | `OK` | No quality rule was triggered. | 99 | | `REVIEW` | At least one rule was triggered: foreground fraction outside 5-95%, intensity range below 10, fewer than 3 slices, image dimensions outside 64-4096 px, or foreground pixels without any contour. | 100 | | `INVALID` | The volume contains no finite values. | 101 | 102 | The thresholds are named constants in `mri_core/decision.py`. Threshold segmentation is not medically validated. 103 | 104 | #### Experimental smoke checkpoint 105 | 106 | - **Purpose.** It exists only to validate the end-to-end software path: local study, model input, checkpoint loading, inference, `DecisionReport`, and Streamlit display. 107 | - **Provenance.** It was trained on CPU for a few seconds using the only 5 fully downloaded labeled studies at the time (3 for training, 2 for validation, 3 epochs). Only the epoch-1 weights were kept, and the validation ROC-AUC from 2 studies is uninformative. It is not a diagnostic or competitively trained model. 108 | - **Availability.** It is generated locally under the git-ignored `outputs/` directory (`outputs/rsna-knee-smoke/checkpoint_smoke.pt`) and is not distributed with the repository. Without it, the app shows `Not available — model checkpoint not loaded`. 109 | - **Opt-in only.** The sidebar checkbox **Use experimental smoke-test checkpoint** is off by default. Enabling it never overwrites or falls back to the normal checkpoint path (`outputs/rsna-knee/checkpoint_best.pt`), and the UI shows: *Experimental smoke-test model — trained on only 3 studies; outputs are not clinically meaningful and are not a diagnosis.* 110 | - **Data scarcity.** Only 58 studies in the RSNA metadata have any labels (see the RSNA adapter section), so any RSNA model trained on this data would rest on at most 58 studies. 111 | 112 | ## Visual walkthrough 113 | 114 | The screenshots below are from the current app running against a locally downloaded RSNA knee MRI study (Explore RSNA Studies mode). 115 | 116 | **Workflow** 117 | 118 | 1. Select a locally available RSNA knee DICOM study. 119 | 2. Select the Axial, Coronal, or Sagittal plane. 120 | 3. Load the multi-slice DICOM volume. 121 | 4. Apply MRI-aware preprocessing to the selected slice. 122 | 5. Generate the segmentation mask and overlay visualization. 123 | 6. Extract deterministic image features. 124 | 7. Optionally enable the experimental smoke checkpoint. 125 | 8. Build the three-plane model input from sampled slices. 126 | 9. Run `RSNAKneeCNN`. 127 | 10. Convert the 12 logits into probabilities. 128 | 11. Generate the deterministic Quality Assessment Report independently of the model. 129 | 12. Present processing, inference, and quality results together in Streamlit. 130 | 131 | ### 1. RSNA DICOM Study Selection 132 | 133 | ![RSNA DICOM Study Selection](docs/images/01-rsna-dicom-study-selection.png) 134 | 135 | *RSNA DICOM Study Selection — Real knee MRI study exploration with plane selection, multi-slice DICOM loading, and the full preprocessing/segmentation workflow visible in a single view.* 136 | 137 | ### 2. MRI Processing Pipeline 138 | 139 | ![MRI Processing Pipeline](docs/images/02-original-preprocessed-mask-overlay.png) 140 | 141 | *MRI Processing Pipeline — Original axial DICOM slice, MRI-aware preprocessing, deterministic segmentation mask, and overlay visualization shown in a compact 2×2 workflow.* 142 | 143 | ### 3. Deterministic Image Features 144 | 145 | ![Deterministic Image Features](docs/images/03-deterministic-image-features.png) 146 | 147 | *Deterministic Image Features — Reproducible measurements extracted from the processed MRI slice, including intensity statistics, foreground coverage, contour area, and bounding geometry.* 148 | 149 | ### 4. 12-Target RSNA Model Inference 150 | 151 | ![12-Target RSNA Model Inference](docs/images/04-12-target-rsna-inference.png) 152 | 153 | *12-Target RSNA Model Inference — Experimental three-plane CNN outputs probabilities for 12 knee abnormality targets, with explicit smoke-test and non-diagnostic warnings.* 154 | 155 | The probabilities shown come from the development smoke checkpoint and demonstrate the inference plumbing only. They are not a measure of clinical performance and must not be read as findings, risks, or predictions about the patient. The smoke checkpoint exists to validate the end-to-end software pipeline; its outputs are not clinically meaningful. 156 | 157 | ### 5. Deterministic Quality Assessment 158 | 159 | ![Deterministic Quality Assessment](docs/images/05-deterministic-quality-assessment.png) 160 | 161 | *Deterministic Quality Assessment — Independent image-quality status and technical metrics remain separate from experimental model predictions, supporting transparent and auditable MRI processing.* 162 | 163 | Quality Status is generated from deterministic image and processing checks (foreground coverage, intensity range, slice count, image size, contour detection, and finite values). It is not changed by the CNN probability outputs: the same study produces the same status whether or not a checkpoint is loaded. 164 | 165 | ### 6. MRI Vision Core End-to-End 166 | 167 | ![MRI Vision Core End-to-End](docs/images/06-mri-vision-core-end-to-end.png) 168 | 169 | *MRI Vision Core End-to-End — RSNA DICOM study selection, preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction, experimental 12-target inference, and deterministic quality assessment integrated into a single Streamlit workflow.* 170 | 171 | > Research and educational prototype. Not for medical diagnosis or clinical decision-making. The smoke checkpoint exists to validate the end-to-end software pipeline; its predictions are not a measure of clinical performance. 172 | 173 | ## Setup and execution 174 | 175 | PowerShell, from the repository root: 176 | 177 | ```powershell 178 | python -m venv .venv 179 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt 180 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m streamlit run app.py 181 | ``` 182 | 183 | Modeling uses scikit-learn (`StandardScaler`, `LogisticRegression`, and `DummyClassifier`); no deep-learning framework is required. 184 | 185 | ## Tests 186 | 187 | The suite collects **74 tests**. The portable default runs **72 synthetic tests**, with **2 optional local MRNet checks skipped**. All 74 passed locally with the dataset enabled before the real baseline was run. 188 | 189 | ```powershell 190 | # Portable CI: no real dataset required or read. 191 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider 192 | 193 | # Opt-in, read-only integration checks at D:\MRI_DATASETS\MRNet. 194 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --run-mrnet 195 | ``` 196 | 197 | Synthetic tests cover shuffled label joins, leading zeros, malformed rows, explicit recovery, duplicates, task mismatch, split overlap, missing planes, ambiguous images, deterministic features, invalid volumes, metric calculations, and the CLI. A leakage regression test changes validation features and labels and confirms that fitted scaler statistics, logistic coefficients, and dummy priors do not change. The synthetic CLI test verifies source-file hashes remain unchanged. 198 | 199 | ## Local MRNet inputs and label validation 200 | 201 | The current local dataset is external to the repository: 202 | 203 | ```text 204 | D:\MRI_DATASETS\MRNet\ 205 | MRNet_ Knee MRI's_files\ 206 | axial\ 0000.npy ... 1249.npy 207 | coronal\ 0000.npy ... 1249.npy 208 | sagittal\ 0000.npy ... 1249.npy 209 | labels\ 210 | train_abnormal.csv 211 | train_acl.csv 212 | train_meniscus.csv 213 | valid_abnormal.csv 214 | valid_acl.csv 215 | valid_meniscus.csv 216 | ``` 217 | 218 | Label files are headerless, two-column `exam_id,label` tables. IDs must be exactly four ASCII digits and remain strings, preserving leading zeros. Labels must be exactly `0` or `1`. Each task must contain the same IDs within its split; duplicate IDs, conflicting records, missing tables, malformed or blank rows, and train/validation overlap are rejected. Row order is irrelevant. Split membership comes from the tables, never ID ranges or folder names. 219 | 220 | The local CSVs have a known first-row anomaly: `"_0000","_1"` in training abnormal, `"_0000","_0"` in the other training tables, and `"_1130","_0"` in all validation tables. Strict mode rejects these rows. **`--recover-first-row` explicitly permits this exact first-row pattern**, removes one leading underscore from both fields in memory, and records the original and recovered values in console output and `report.json`. It never silently discards a row, treats it as a header, or edits a source CSV. Ordinary headerless tables need no compatibility option. 221 | 222 | The resulting manifest has one row per examination with: 223 | 224 | ```text 225 | exam_id,split,axial_available,coronal_available,sagittal_available,abnormal,acl,meniscus 226 | ``` 227 | 228 | Image paths are resolved separately from all matching plane directories, including nested split layouts. Duplicate ID/plane files are rejected. Missing and unlabeled images are reported; the baseline refuses to fit until the mapping is complete. CSV consumers must read `exam_id` as text to retain leading zeros. 229 | 230 | ## First predictive baseline 231 | 232 | ```powershell 233 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m mri_core.baseline ` 234 | --dataset-root D:\MRI_DATASETS\MRNet ` 235 | --labels-dir D:\MRI_DATASETS\MRNet\labels ` 236 | --output-dir outputs\v0.4 ` 237 | --recover-first-row 238 | ``` 239 | 240 | Omit `--recover-first-row` for standard CSVs. `--labels-dir` defaults to `/labels`. The dataset is optional for installing the project and running CI. 241 | 242 | Feature extraction opens external `.npy` arrays with `mmap_mode="r"` and `allow_pickle=False`, using axis 0 as the slice axis. Each plane contributes nine evenly spaced slices including endpoints, or all slices for shorter volumes. Each slice is independently clipped and normalized using its 1st/99th percentiles; a constant slice becomes zero. Sampled slices must be finite, numeric, and at least 2×2. 243 | 244 | Ten slice statistics are computed: intensity mean, standard deviation, 10th/50th/90th percentiles, 32-bin entropy, gradient magnitude mean/standard deviation/90th percentile, and fraction of pixels with gradient magnitude above 0.1. Means and standard deviations across sampled slices yield 20 features per plane. Concatenating axial, coronal, and sagittal features gives **60 features per examination**. Normalization uses only the current slice; it learns no population parameters. 245 | 246 | For each target, a separate `StandardScaler` → `LogisticRegression` pipeline uses fixed `C=1.0`, `class_weight="balanced"`, `solver="lbfgs"`, `max_iter=2000`, and `random_state=0`. A `DummyClassifier(strategy="prior")` provides a comparison. **Only training examinations are passed to every `.fit()` call**, including scaling, class weights, and dummy priors. Validation is used once for evaluation, without hyperparameter search, calibration, or threshold tuning. All binary metrics use a fixed probability threshold of **0.5**. Nonconvergence stops execution. 247 | 248 | Derived artifacts are written under ignored `outputs/v0.4/`: 249 | 250 | - `manifest.csv`: labels, splits, and plane availability. 251 | - `features.csv`: examination IDs, splits, and 60 numeric features. 252 | - `report.json`: class distributions, logistic/dummy metrics, recovery records, source label SHA-256 hashes, timings, configuration, feature names, software versions, and limitations. 253 | 254 | No MRI arrays are copied into the repository. The CLI rejects output locations overlapping source directories. Feature extraction time covers image reads and feature calculation; training time covers all three scaler/logistic fits and three dummy fits, excluding evaluation and artifact writing. 255 | 256 | Metrics include ROC-AUC, average precision, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and confusion matrices in **`[[TN, FP], [FN, TP]]`** order. Undefined ROC-AUC/AP values are JSON `null` with explanatory notes. Precision/recall/F1 use `zero_division=0`, also reported in notes when applicable. 257 | 258 | ## Local V0.4 results 259 | 260 | The 2026-09-19 run used 1,250 examinations: **1,130 train / 120 validation**, with all three planes available for every exam (3,750 external image files). There were no missing or unlabeled exams and no split overlap. Six first-row recoveries were explicitly recorded; no source labels were rewritten. 261 | 262 | | Target | Train negative / positive | Train prevalence | Validation negative / positive | Validation prevalence | 263 | |---|---|---:|---|---:| 264 | | Abnormal | 217 / 913 | 80.80% | 25 / 95 | 79.17% | 265 | | ACL | 922 / 208 | 18.41% | 66 / 54 | 45.00% | 266 | | Meniscus | 733 / 397 | 35.13% | 68 / 52 | 43.33% | 267 | 268 | Validation metrics at the fixed 0.5 threshold (AP = average precision): 269 | 270 | | Target | Model | ROC-AUC | AP | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | Confusion matrix | 271 | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| 272 | | Abnormal | Logistic | 0.8552 | 0.9365 | 0.8167 | 0.9294 | 0.8316 | 0.8778 | `[[19,6],[16,79]]` | 273 | | Abnormal | Dummy | 0.5000 | 0.7917 | 0.7917 | 0.7917 | 1.0000 | 0.8837 | `[[0,25],[0,95]]` | 274 | | ACL | Logistic | 0.8171 | 0.7877 | 0.7417 | 0.7091 | 0.7222 | 0.7156 | `[[50,16],[15,39]]` | 275 | | ACL | Dummy | 0.5000 | 0.4500 | 0.5500 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | `[[66,0],[54,0]]` | 276 | | Meniscus | Logistic | 0.7240 | 0.6239 | 0.6667 | 0.5909 | 0.7500 | 0.6610 | `[[41,27],[13,39]]` | 277 | | Meniscus | Dummy | 0.5000 | 0.4333 | 0.5667 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | `[[68,0],[52,0]]` | 278 | 279 | The ACL and meniscus dummy models predict no positives; their precision is set to zero with an explicit note in the report. Logistic regression improves ranking metrics and accuracy for all three targets, but the always-positive abnormality dummy has slightly higher F1. No settings were adjusted after observing these results. 280 | 281 | Feature extraction took **179.205 seconds**; training the three scaled logistic models and three dummy models took **0.106 seconds** on this machine. These are single-run wall-clock measurements, not benchmark guarantees. The run used Python 3.12.10, NumPy 2.5.3, and scikit-learn 1.9.1. Exact metrics and provenance are in the locally generated, ignored `outputs/v0.4/report.json`. 282 | 283 | ## Limitations 284 | 285 | - Handcrafted slice summaries do not localize tears or provide diagnostic evidence; sampled slices may miss focal findings. 286 | - Per-slice normalization removes absolute intensity scale. Planes are concatenated, not spatially registered. 287 | - The validation set has only 120 examinations; there are no confidence intervals or independent external test results. 288 | - ACL prevalence differs substantially between training and validation. Fixed balanced weights do not establish calibrated probabilities. 289 | - Examination IDs are separated across splits; this does not verify patient-level independence. 290 | - The UI's threshold segmentation remains separate from the predictive baseline and is not medically validated. 291 | 292 | Future work should evaluate stronger features and robustness without repeatedly tuning against this validation split. ROI tools, deep segmentation, volumetric radiomics, and an API remain possible later milestones. 293 | 294 | ## RSNA Knee Abnormality Detection adapter 295 | 296 | The RSNA adapter is metadata-first and supports the verified CSV layout under `data/rsna-knee/` without requiring the approximately 570 GB DICOM collection. It preserves `StudyInstanceUID` and `SeriesInstanceUID` as strings, groups series by study, exposes `Fluid_Sensitive`, `Fat_Suppression`, and `Anatomical_Plane`, and reports whether `train_series///` and `test_series///` exist. The exact 12 targets are `ACL`, `MCL`, `Medial Meniscus`, `Lateral Meniscus`, `Medial OA`, `Lateral OA`, `PF OA`, `Effusion`, `Synovitis`, `Baker's`, `Contusion`, and `Fracture`. 297 | 298 | The current local metadata inspection found **4,407 training studies**, **3 test studies**, and **24,371 training series**. Series per study range from 3 to 14, with mean 5.5301 and median 5. The series counts are Sagittal 9,864, Coronal 8,609, and Axial 5,898. Fluid-sensitive counts are 14,010 true / 10,361 false; fat-suppression counts are 14,010 true / 10,361 false. Only **58 studies have complete 12-target labels**; 4,349 rows have every target missing. Training must therefore use only complete-label studies and must not treat missing labels as negatives. 299 | 300 | Inspect metadata now: 301 | 302 | ```powershell 303 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B scripts\kaggle_rsna_knee.py inspect --data-dir data\rsna-knee 304 | ``` 305 | 306 | With DICOM data attached later, the future commands are: 307 | 308 | ```powershell 309 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B scripts\kaggle_rsna_knee.py train --data-dir --config configs\rsna_knee.json 310 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B scripts\kaggle_rsna_knee.py evaluate --data-dir --checkpoint 311 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B scripts\kaggle_rsna_knee.py submit --data-dir --checkpoint --output submission.csv 312 | ``` 313 | 314 | The model reuses the V0.5 shared encoder with a 12-logit head and applies one sigmoid probability per target. Training uses study-level splitting, `BCEWithLogitsLoss`, the configured seed, CUDA when available, CPU otherwise, and best-checkpoint selection by macro ROC-AUC. Per-label ROC-AUC is reported when both validation classes are present; single-class validation labels are reported as unavailable instead of raising. Submission generation takes the exact column order and study IDs from `sample_submission.csv`. Source CSVs, DICOM directories, checkpoints, and generated submissions are ignored by Git. 315 | 316 | ## V0.5 CNN experiment 317 | 318 | V0.5 adds an optional PyTorch path that is separate from Streamlit and preserves the V0.4 handcrafted-feature baseline. Install the optional dependency in a separate environment; the base `requirements.txt` does not require PyTorch: 319 | 320 | ```powershell 321 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-cnn.txt 322 | ``` 323 | 324 | The reference CNN uses a shared four-block 2D encoder (16, 32, 64, and 128 channels), GroupNorm, ReLU, spatial mean pooling, masked max pooling across nine sampled slices, plane concatenation, dropout, and three independent logits for abnormality, ACL tear, and meniscal tear. It has 97,779 trainable parameters in the reference configuration. Inputs are grayscale, 128×128, and use the existing per-slice 1st/99th percentile normalization. Training augmentation applies one deterministic affine/contrast transform to all slices of a plane; validation has no augmentation. BCE-with-logits uses positive weights computed from training labels only. 325 | 326 | Local execution is intentionally limited to synthetic CPU smoke tests. Full MRNet training refuses CPU and requires CUDA. The CPU smoke command creates temporary synthetic arrays and labels, then verifies dataset tensors, forward/loss/backward/optimizer behavior, checkpoint reload, prediction generation, and metrics: 327 | 328 | ```powershell 329 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m mri_core.cnn_train smoke 330 | ``` 331 | 332 | The Kaggle-ready entrypoint is `scripts/kaggle_cnn.py`. Attach the Stanford arrays and six label CSVs as a Kaggle input dataset; keep the source files under `/kaggle/input` and write derived artifacts under `/kaggle/working`. Select the documented NVIDIA T4×2 accelerator, use `cuda:0`, and run the one-epoch benchmark first: 333 | 334 | ```bash 335 | pip install -r requirements-cnn.txt 336 | python scripts/kaggle_cnn.py benchmark \ 337 | --dataset-root /kaggle/input/mrnet/MRNet_ Knee MRI's_files \ 338 | --labels-dir /kaggle/input/mrnet/labels \ 339 | --output-root /kaggle/working/outputs/v0.5 \ 340 | --recover-first-row 341 | ``` 342 | 343 | After inspecting the benchmark report, launch the fixed three-seed experiment with the same paths: 344 | 345 | ```bash 346 | python scripts/kaggle_cnn.py train \ 347 | --dataset-root /kaggle/input/mrnet/MRNet_ Knee MRI's_files \ 348 | --labels-dir /kaggle/input/mrnet/labels \ 349 | --output-root /kaggle/working/outputs/v0.5 \ 350 | --recover-first-row 351 | ``` 352 | 353 | The benchmark and training commands require the V0.4 manifest fingerprint and exact 1,130/120 train/validation split. They reject missing or unlabeled images, split changes, and CPU full runs. Each run records its config, source hashes, environment, sampling indices, checkpoints, predictions, losses, timings, and per-seed comparison metrics under the output directory. No source arrays or CSVs are copied into Git. 354 | 355 | Planning estimates for the reference configuration are 10–45 minutes for the three-plane, 20-epoch run on a typical Kaggle T4-class GPU, 2–4 GB VRAM, and roughly 1–3 MB per checkpoint. The first epoch benchmark replaces these estimates with measured timing and peak CUDA memory. The current local machine has no CUDA-capable PyTorch device, so no real-data CNN run has been started. 356 |

2 | 
3 | Reuses the existing dataset preparation, model architecture, and exception framework

19 | # Reuse existing exception classes from rsna_knee_inference
20 | from .rsna_knee_inference import (
21 |     CheckpointNotFoundError,

31 | def run_ensemble_inference(
32 |     metadata: RSNAKneeMetadata,
33 |     fold_checkpoint_paths: Sequence[Path | str],
34 |     study_uid: str,
35 |     config: Optional[dict] = None,
36 |     device: str = "cpu",
37 | ) -> Dict[str, float]:
38 |     """Run one study through all five folds and return ensemble-averaged probabilities.
39 | 
40 |     Args:
41 |         metadata: Loaded RSNA metadata (from load_rsna_metadata / load_rsna_metadata_safe).
42 |         fold_checkpoint_paths: Sequence of exactly 5 checkpoint paths, one per fold.
43 |             Each must be a file saved by rsna_knee_train.train_rsna.
44 |         study_uid: StudyInstanceUID to run inference on. Must have a labeled row in
45 |             metadata.train and locally available DICOMs.
46 |         config: Optional override for dataset preparation. Defaults to the first
47 |             fold checkpoint's config, keeping input shape consistent with training.
48 |         device: Torch device string. Inference always loads checkpoints on CPU first;
49 |             this only controls where the forward pass runs.
50 | 
51 |     Returns:
52 |         Dict mapping each of the 12 TARGET_COLUMNS (in that exact order) to the
53 |         arithmetic mean of the sigmoid probability across all five folds.
54 | 
55 |     Raises:
56 |         CheckpointNotFoundError, MalformedCheckpointError, TargetMismatchError,
57 |         ArchitectureMismatchError, StudyUnavailableError.
58 | 
59 |     Note:
60 |         All five checkpoints are validated before any inference occurs. If any
61 |         checkpoint is missing, invalid, or incompatible, an exception is raised
62 |         without returning a partial ensemble.
63 |     """
64 |     fold_checkpoint_paths = [Path(p) for p in fold_checkpoint_paths]
65 |     if len(fold_checkpoint_paths) != 5:
66 |         raise ValueError(
67 |             f"Expected exactly 5 fold checkpoint paths, got {len(fold_checkpoint_paths)}"
68 |         )
69 | 
70 |     # ======================================================================
71 |     # Phase 1: Validate all five checkpoints upfront (fail-fast)
72 |     # ======================================================================
73 |     loaded_checkpoints = []
74 |     models = []
75 | 
76 |     for fold_idx, checkpoint_path in enumerate(fold_checkpoint_paths, start=1):
77 |         checkpoint_path = Path(checkpoint_path)
78 |         if not checkpoint_path.is_file():
79 |             raise CheckpointNotFoundError(
80 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: No checkpoint file at {checkpoint_path}"
81 |             )
82 | 
83 |         try:
84 |             checkpoint_data = torch.load(
85 |                 checkpoint_path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True
86 |             )
87 |         except Exception as exc:
88 |             raise MalformedCheckpointError(
89 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: Failed to load checkpoint {checkpoint_path}: {exc}"
90 |             ) from exc
91 | 
92 |         if not isinstance(checkpoint_data, dict):
93 |             raise MalformedCheckpointError(
94 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: Checkpoint did not contain a dict "
95 |                 f"(got {type(checkpoint_data).__name__})"
96 |             )
97 | 
98 |         missing_keys = [
99 |             key for key in REQUIRED_CHECKPOINT_KEYS if key not in checkpoint_data
100 |         ]
101 |         if missing_keys:
102 |             raise MalformedCheckpointError(
103 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: Checkpoint is missing required fields: {missing_keys}"
104 |             )
105 | 
106 |         # Validate target columns
107 |         target_columns = checkpoint_data["target_columns"]
108 |         if list(target_columns) != list(TARGET_COLUMNS):
109 |             raise TargetMismatchError(
110 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: target_columns {list(target_columns)!r} "
111 |                 f"do not match expected TARGET_COLUMNS {list(TARGET_COLUMNS)!r}"
112 |             )
113 | 
114 |         # Validate and extract config
115 |         checkpoint_config = checkpoint_data["config"]
116 |         if not isinstance(checkpoint_config, dict):
117 |             raise MalformedCheckpointError(
118 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: 'config' field is not a dict "
119 |                 f"(got {type(checkpoint_config).__name__})"
120 |             )
121 | 
122 |         try:
123 |             # Support both Kaggle format (num_planes) and existing format (planes list)
124 |             if "planes" in checkpoint_config:
125 |                 planes = tuple(checkpoint_config.get("planes", ("Axial", "Coronal", "Sagittal")))
126 |                 num_planes = len(planes)
127 |             else:
128 |                 num_planes = int(checkpoint_config.get("num_planes", 3))
129 |                 planes = None
130 |             dropout = float(checkpoint_config["dropout"])
131 |         except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
132 |             raise MalformedCheckpointError(
133 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: 'config' is incomplete or invalid: {exc}"
134 |             ) from exc
135 | 
136 |         # Instantiate model
137 |         try:
138 |             model = RSNAKneeCNN(num_planes=num_planes, dropout=dropout)
139 |         except ValueError as exc:
140 |             raise MalformedCheckpointError(
141 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: config produced an invalid model: {exc}"
142 |             ) from exc
143 | 
144 |         # Load state dict
145 |         if not isinstance(checkpoint_data["model"], dict):
146 |             raise MalformedCheckpointError(
147 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: 'model' field is not a state dict "
148 |                 f"(got {type(checkpoint_data['model']).__name__})"
149 |             )
150 | 
151 |         try:
152 |             model.load_state_dict(checkpoint_data["model"])
153 |         except (RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
154 |             raise ArchitectureMismatchError(
155 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: weights are not compatible with the current "
156 |                 f"RSNAKneeCNN: {exc}"
157 |             ) from exc
158 | 
159 |         model.eval()
160 |         try:
161 |             torch_device = torch.device(device)
162 |             model = model.to(torch_device)
163 |         except (RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
164 |             raise RSNAInferenceError(
165 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: Could not move model to device {device!r}: {exc}"
166 |             ) from exc
167 | 
168 |         loaded_checkpoints.append(checkpoint_data)
169 |         models.append(model)
170 | 
171 |     # ======================================================================
172 |     # Phase 2: Prepare the study (deterministic, once)
173 |     # ======================================================================
174 |     study_rows = metadata.train[
175 |         metadata.train["StudyInstanceUID"].astype(str) == str(study_uid)
176 |     ]
177 |     if study_rows.empty:
178 |         raise StudyUnavailableError(
179 |             f"StudyInstanceUID={study_uid} has no labeled row in metadata.train"
180 |         )
181 | 
182 |     # Use first checkpoint's config as default; allow override
183 |     raw_config = (
184 |         config if config is not None else loaded_checkpoints[0]["config"]
185 |     )
186 | 
187 |     # Normalize config for dataset preparation:
188 |     # - Kaggle checkpoints use 'slices_per_plane' but dataset expects 'slices_per_series'
189 |     # - Support both 'planes' list and 'num_planes' int formats
190 |     effective_config = dict(raw_config)
191 |     if "slices_per_series" not in effective_config and "slices_per_plane" in effective_config:
192 |         effective_config["slices_per_series"] = effective_config["slices_per_plane"]
193 | 
194 |     try:
195 |         dataset = RSNAKneeDicomDataset(
196 |             metadata, study_rows, effective_config, split="train"
197 |         )
198 |         item = dataset[0]
199 |     except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError, KeyError, DicomSeriesError) as exc:
200 |         raise StudyUnavailableError(
201 |             f"StudyInstanceUID={study_uid}: could not prepare study for inference: {exc}"
202 |         ) from exc
203 | 
204 |     images = item["images"].unsqueeze(0).to(torch_device)
205 |     mask = item["mask"].unsqueeze(0).to(torch_device)
206 | 
207 |     # ======================================================================
208 |     # Phase 3: Run through all five models and collect probabilities
209 |     # ======================================================================
210 |     fold_probabilities = []
211 | 
212 |     for fold_idx, model in enumerate(models, start=1):
213 |         try:
214 |             with torch.inference_mode():
215 |                 logits = model(images, mask)
216 |                 probabilities = logits.sigmoid().squeeze(0).cpu().numpy()
217 |         except (RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
218 |             raise ArchitectureMismatchError(
219 |                 f"Fold {fold_idx}: Forward pass failed for StudyInstanceUID={study_uid}; "
220 |                 f"the checkpoint's architecture may not match the prepared input: {exc}"
221 |             ) from exc
222 | 
223 |         fold_probabilities.append(probabilities)
224 | 
225 |     # ======================================================================
226 |     # Phase 4: Ensemble output (arithmetic mean)
227 |     # ======================================================================
228 |     ensemble_probabilities = np.mean(fold_probabilities, axis=0)
229 | 
230 |     return {
231 |         target: float(ensemble_probabilities[index])
232 |         for index, target in enumerate(TARGET_COLUMNS)
233 |     }

1 | """Approximately 100k-parameter slice encoder and multilabel exam classifier."""
2 | 
3 | import torch
4 | from torch import nn
5 | 
6 | 
7 | class MRNetCNN(nn.Module):
8 |     def __init__(self, num_planes=3, dropout=0.2, num_targets=3):
9 |         super().__init__()
10 |         if num_planes not in (1, 2, 3):
11 |             raise ValueError("Expected one to three planes")
12 |         if type(num_targets) is not int or num_targets < 1:
13 |             raise ValueError("Expected a positive target count")
14 |         self.num_planes = num_planes
15 |         self.num_targets = num_targets
16 |         blocks, previous = [], 1
17 |         for channels in (16, 32, 64, 128):
18 |             blocks.extend([nn.Conv2d(previous, channels, 3, stride=2, padding=1, bias=False),
19 |                            nn.GroupNorm(8, channels), nn.ReLU()])
20 |             previous = channels
21 |         self.encoder = nn.Sequential(*blocks)
22 |         self.head = nn.Sequential(nn.Dropout(dropout), nn.Linear(128 * num_planes, num_targets))
23 | 
24 |     def forward(self, images, mask):
25 |         if images.ndim != 6 or images.shape[1] != self.num_planes or images.shape[3] != 1:
26 |             raise ValueError("Expected [batch, planes, slices, 1, height, width]")
27 |         if mask.shape != images.shape[:3] or mask.dtype != torch.bool or not mask.any(dim=2).all():
28 |             raise ValueError("Each exam plane requires at least one valid slice")
29 |         # Padding never enters the encoder and cannot affect pooling or normalization.
30 |         # Explicit spatial mean avoids nondeterministic CUDA adaptive-pooling backward kernels.
31 |         embeddings = self.encoder(images[mask]).mean(dim=(-2, -1))
32 |         expanded = embeddings.new_full((*mask.shape, 128), -torch.inf)
33 |         expanded[mask] = embeddings
34 |         pooled = expanded.max(dim=2).values.flatten(start_dim=1)
35 |         return self.head(pooled)

---

## MRI ChangeGuard / Clinical Decision-Support — Implementation Brief

### Current Architecture

A layered Streamlit app ([`app.py`](app.py)) over a classical image-processing core ([`mri_core/pipeline.py`](mri_core/pipeline.py)), a handcrafted-feature logistic baseline ([`mri_core/baseline.py`](mri_core/baseline.py)), and an optional PyTorch CNN path ([`mri_core/rsna_knee_model.py`](mri_core/rsna_knee_model.py)). Inputs are DICOM, NIfTI, NumPy, or PNG/JPG. Two strictly separated result paths — a deterministic image-quality report ([`mri_core/decision.py`](mri_core/decision.py)) and an experimental 12-target CNN probability block — are merged only in [`DecisionReport`](mri_core/decision.py:54), which is a frozen dataclass. The CNN is a shallow 4-block 2D encoder (~102k params, 128×128 grayscale, 3-plane, 9 slices/plane) with a logistic head; a 5-fold ensemble wrapper ([`mri_core/rsna_knee_ensemble.py`](mri_core/rsna_knee_ensemble.py)) is complete. The MRNet handcrafted baseline runs separately via CLI and is not surfaced in the UI. Test coverage is 74 tests (72 synthetic CI, 2 optional local).

---

### What Already Works

1. **Full DICOM ingestion pipeline** — series ordering, plane selection, fluid-sensitive series preference, volume assembly.
2. **Classical preprocessing, segmentation, overlay, and feature extraction** — deterministic, reproducible, and audit-logged.
3. **Deterministic quality gating** — `OK / REVIEW / INVALID` computed from foreground fraction, intensity range, slice count, dimension bounds, and contour detection; never affected by the model.
4. **MRNet handcrafted baseline** — 60-feature LogReg pipeline, train-only fitting, held-out metrics (ACL ROC-AUC 0.82, Abnormal 0.86), reproducible CLI, `report.json` with hashes.
5. **RSNA 12-target CNN** — architecture, dataset class, training loop, inference entry-point, checkpoint format, and single-study inference are all complete.
6. **5-fold ensemble inference** — fail-fast checkpoint validation and arithmetic-mean averaging are implemented and UI-selectable.
7. **`DecisionReport` container** — immutable, stores quality and model predictions in separate fields, validates probability bounds on ingestion.
8. **74-test synthetic suite** — covers edge cases in label parsing, manifest joining, baseline leakage, DICOM series selection, inference, and end-to-end UI layout.

---

### Gaps Relative to a Credible Demo

1. **No real trained checkpoint exists.** The only checkpoint is a 3-study smoke artifact. The 5-fold ensemble paths in `app.py` point to `outputs/rsna-knee-ensemble/` which cannot be populated without CUDA training on the 58 complete-label RSNA studies. Without a checkpoint, the "predictions" panel is always blank — the centerpiece of the demo is absent.
2. **58 labeled studies is too small for 12 targets.** Many targets (MCL, Baker's, Fracture, Synovitis) will have near-zero prevalence; single-class validation will suppress per-label AUC. This is structurally acknowledged but not addressed.
3. **The two result paths are never integrated.** `DecisionReport` stores quality and probabilities in adjacent fields but they do not inform each other — there is no risk stratification rule, alert tier, or combined summary sentence. A clinician-facing tool needs a synthesized output, not two parallel tables.
4. **Probability display is a raw table.** Twelve floating-point numbers in a `st.dataframe` give no clinical framing: no threshold line, no change-from-baseline (the "ChangeGuard" concept), no ordering by concern level, no uncertainty estimate.
5. **No longitudinal or comparison mode.** The app loads a single study; there is no concept of "prior" vs "current" to implement the ChangeGuard differential. This is the biggest architectural gap relative to the stated name.
6. **No ROI visualization.** Segmentation exists but outputs only a global foreground mask; focal anatomy (ACL, meniscus horn, joint space) is never localized or overlaid, so model output cannot be spatially grounded.
7. **Baseline and CNN outputs are never shown together.** The handcrafted LogReg predictions (available from `baseline.py`) are not surfaced in the UI alongside the CNN — a useful cross-validation signal for a demo audience is invisible.

---

### Smallest High-Impact Next Feature

**Risk-stratified synthesis layer in `DecisionReport` + a single-sentence alert in the UI.**

Concretely: add a `risk_tier` field (`LOW / ELEVATED / HIGH`) to [`DecisionReport`](mri_core/decision.py:54) computed from the probability dict — e.g., any target > 0.7 → `HIGH`, any > 0.4 → `ELEVATED`, else `LOW` — and replace the raw probability table in [`app.py`](app.py:328) with a color-coded metric tile (`🔴 HIGH – ACL 0.82, Effusion 0.74`) above the full table. This requires zero new data, zero new training, zero new modules, closes the "two parallel tables" gap immediately, gives the demo a legible headline finding, and demonstrates the clinical decision-support framing that justifies the "ChangeGuard" name — all in ~20 lines across two files.

Implement the smallest credible deterministic “ChangeGuard Comparison” feature.

Keep the existing single-study flow unchanged. Add an optional Prior Study input alongside Current Study. When both are supplied, reuse the existing loading, preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction, and quality-gate paths for each study, then produce a frozen comparison result containing:
- quality status for each study
- auditable numeric changes in already-available image/segmentation features
- a conservative status: STABLE or REVIEW, with explicit reason strings
- a clear UI section titled “ChangeGuard comparison — non-diagnostic; clinician review required”

Show current/prior overlays or representative images side-by-side when available. Add focused synthetic tests for stable, review, missing-prior, and invalid-quality cases.

Do not use or modify CNN probabilities, do not install packages, do not use Groq/Grafana/external services, and do not make clinical diagnostic claims. """Deterministic ChangeGuard comparison layer.

Compares two DecisionReport objects (prior vs current) using only the
image-derived features and quality statuses already present in each report.

No CNN probabilities are read or modified.  No medical claims are made.
Every REVIEW reason string explicitly states it is an image-derived change
candidate requiring clinician review, not a clinical finding or diagnosis.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import List

from .decision import DecisionReport, QualityStatus


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Thresholds — named constants so they are easy to audit and adjust.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Absolute change in foreground fraction (0-1 scale) that warrants REVIEW.
FOREGROUND_FRACTION_REVIEW_THRESHOLD = 0.15  # 15 percentage points

# Absolute change in mean intensity (0-255 uint8 scale) that warrants REVIEW.
MEAN_INTENSITY_REVIEW_THRESHOLD = 20.0

# Absolute change in foreground pixel count (fraction of total pixels) — secondary guard.
FOREGROUND_PIXEL_FRACTION_REVIEW_THRESHOLD = 0.15


class ComparisonStatus(str, Enum):
    """Outcome of a ChangeGuard comparison run."""
    STABLE = "STABLE"
    REVIEW = "REVIEW"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FeatureDelta:
    """Auditable numeric change for one image-derived feature between two studies.

    All values are image-pipeline outputs; none are clinical measurements.
    """
    feature: str
    prior_value: float
    current_value: float
    absolute_change: float   # current − prior
    relative_change: float   # (current − prior) / |prior|, or 0.0 when prior is 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ComparisonReport:
    """Immutable result of a deterministic ChangeGuard comparison.

    This report describes image-derived feature changes between two studies.
    It does not constitute a clinical finding, diagnosis, or medical opinion.
    Clinician review is required before any clinical action is taken.
    """

    prior_study_uid: str
    current_study_uid: str
    prior_quality_status: QualityStatus
    current_quality_status: QualityStatus

    # Ordered list of auditable per-feature deltas.
    feature_deltas: List[FeatureDelta] = field(default_factory=list)

    # Comparison outcome.
    status: ComparisonStatus = ComparisonStatus.STABLE

    # Human-readable reasons for REVIEW status (empty when STABLE).
    # Every string explicitly states this is an image-derived change candidate,
    # not a clinical finding or diagnosis.
    reasons: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def _delta(feature: str, prior: float, current: float) -> FeatureDelta:
    """Build a FeatureDelta from two scalar values."""
    absolute = current - prior
    relative = absolute / abs(prior) if prior != 0.0 else 0.0
    return FeatureDelta(
        feature=feature,
        prior_value=prior,
        current_value=current,
        absolute_change=absolute,
        relative_change=relative,
    )


def generate_comparison_report(
    prior: DecisionReport,
    current: DecisionReport,
) -> ComparisonReport:
    """Produce a frozen ComparisonReport from two DecisionReport objects.

    Args:
        prior: DecisionReport from the earlier (reference) study.
        current: DecisionReport from the study being reviewed.

    Returns:
        ComparisonReport — always frozen, always auditable.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If either study has QualityStatus.INVALID.  Comparison of
            corrupt or non-finite data cannot produce a meaningful result.
    """
    if prior.quality_status == QualityStatus.INVALID:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cannot compare: prior study {prior.study_uid!r} has INVALID quality status. "
            "Load a study with OK or REVIEW quality as the prior."
        )
    if current.quality_status == QualityStatus.INVALID:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cannot compare: current study {current.study_uid!r} has INVALID quality status. "
            "The current study must have OK or REVIEW quality to run a comparison."
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Build auditable per-feature deltas from image-pipeline measurements.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    prior_qm = prior.quality_metrics
    current_qm = current.quality_metrics
    prior_sq = prior.segmentation_quality
    current_sq = current.segmentation_quality

    deltas: List[FeatureDelta] = [
        _delta("mean_intensity",        prior_qm.mean_intensity,        current_qm.mean_intensity),
        _delta("std_intensity",         prior_qm.std_intensity,         current_qm.std_intensity),
        _delta("intensity_range",       prior_qm.intensity_range,       current_qm.intensity_range),
        _delta("foreground_fraction",   prior_sq.foreground_fraction,   current_sq.foreground_fraction),
        _delta("foreground_pixels",     float(prior_sq.foreground_pixels), float(current_sq.foreground_pixels)),
        _delta("largest_contour_area",  prior_sq.largest_contour_area,  current_sq.largest_contour_area),
    ]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Evaluate REVIEW rules — each rule appends a reason string that
    # explicitly labels it as an image-derived change candidate.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reasons: List[str] = []

    ff_delta = abs(current_sq.foreground_fraction - prior_sq.foreground_fraction)
    if ff_delta >= FOREGROUND_FRACTION_REVIEW_THRESHOLD:
        reasons.append(
            f"Image-derived change candidate: foreground fraction shifted by "
            f"{ff_delta * 100:.1f} percentage points "
            f"(prior {prior_sq.foreground_fraction * 100:.1f}% → "
            f"current {current_sq.foreground_fraction * 100:.1f}%). "
            "This is a segmentation measurement change, not a clinical finding or diagnosis. "
            "Clinician review required."
        )

    mi_delta = abs(current_qm.mean_intensity - prior_qm.mean_intensity)
    if mi_delta >= MEAN_INTENSITY_REVIEW_THRESHOLD:
        reasons.append(
            f"Image-derived change candidate: mean intensity shifted by "
            f"{mi_delta:.1f} units "
            f"(prior {prior_qm.mean_intensity:.1f} → current {current_qm.mean_intensity:.1f}). "
            "This is a pixel-level measurement change, not a clinical finding or diagnosis. "
            "Clinician review required."
        )

    if prior.quality_status != QualityStatus.OK:
        reasons.append(
            f"Image-derived change candidate: prior study quality status is "
            f"{prior.quality_status.value!r} (not OK) — image-quality flags: "
            f"{'; '.join(prior.quality_flags) or 'none recorded'}. "
            "Comparison reliability may be reduced. Clinician review required."
        )

    if current.quality_status != QualityStatus.OK:
        reasons.append(
            f"Image-derived change candidate: current study quality status is "
            f"{current.quality_status.value!r} (not OK) — image-quality flags: "
            f"{'; '.join(current.quality_flags) or 'none recorded'}. "
            "Comparison reliability may be reduced. Clinician review required."
        )

    status = ComparisonStatus.REVIEW if reasons else ComparisonStatus.STABLE

    return ComparisonReport(
        prior_study_uid=prior.study_uid,
        current_study_uid=current.study_uid,
        prior_quality_status=prior.quality_status,
        current_quality_status=current.quality_status,
        feature_deltas=deltas,
        status=status,
        reasons=reasons,
    )

"""Synthetic tests for the ChangeGuard deterministic comparison layer.

All tests are self-contained; no real dataset, DICOM files, or network access
is required.  Fixtures build minimal DecisionReport objects from known values.
"""

import numpy as np
import pytest

from mri_core.comparison import (
    ComparisonReport,
    ComparisonStatus,
    FeatureDelta,
    FOREGROUND_FRACTION_REVIEW_THRESHOLD,
    MEAN_INTENSITY_REVIEW_THRESHOLD,
    generate_comparison_report,
)
from mri_core.decision import (
    DecisionReport,
    ImageQualityMetrics,
    QualityStatus,
    SegmentationQuality,
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _metrics(
    mean_intensity: float = 128.0,
    std_intensity: float = 30.0,
    min_intensity: float = 10.0,
    max_intensity: float = 240.0,
    intensity_range: float = 230.0,
    foreground_fraction: float = 0.40,
) -> ImageQualityMetrics:
    return ImageQualityMetrics(
        mean_intensity=mean_intensity,
        std_intensity=std_intensity,
        min_intensity=min_intensity,
        max_intensity=max_intensity,
        intensity_range=intensity_range,
        foreground_fraction=foreground_fraction,
    )


def _seg(
    foreground_pixels: int = 26214,  # ~40% of 256x256
    foreground_fraction: float = 0.40,
    largest_contour_area: float = 25000.0,
    has_contours: bool = True,
) -> SegmentationQuality:
    return SegmentationQuality(
        foreground_pixels=foreground_pixels,
        foreground_fraction=foreground_fraction,
        largest_contour_area=largest_contour_area,
        has_contours=has_contours,
    )


def _report(
    study_uid: str = "1.2.3",
    series_uid: str = "4.5.6",
    plane: str = "Axial",
    num_slices: int = 20,
    quality_status: QualityStatus = QualityStatus.OK,
    quality_flags: list = None,
    quality_metrics: ImageQualityMetrics = None,
    segmentation_quality: SegmentationQuality = None,
) -> DecisionReport:
    return DecisionReport(
        study_uid=study_uid,
        series_uid=series_uid,
        plane=plane,
        num_slices=num_slices,
        image_height=256,
        image_width=256,
        quality_metrics=quality_metrics or _metrics(),
        segmentation_quality=segmentation_quality or _seg(),
        quality_status=quality_status,
        quality_flags=quality_flags or [],
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ComparisonStatus enum
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestComparisonStatus:
    def test_enum_values(self):
        assert ComparisonStatus.STABLE.value == "STABLE"
        assert ComparisonStatus.REVIEW.value == "REVIEW"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FeatureDelta immutability
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestFeatureDelta:
    def test_frozen(self):
        delta = FeatureDelta(
            feature="mean_intensity",
            prior_value=100.0,
            current_value=120.0,
            absolute_change=20.0,
            relative_change=0.2,
        )
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            delta.prior_value = 0.0  # type: ignore[misc]

    def test_values(self):
        delta = FeatureDelta(
            feature="foreground_fraction",
            prior_value=0.4,
            current_value=0.6,
            absolute_change=0.2,
            relative_change=0.5,
        )
        assert delta.absolute_change == pytest.approx(0.2)
        assert delta.relative_change == pytest.approx(0.5)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ComparisonReport immutability
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestComparisonReport:
    def test_frozen(self):
        report = ComparisonReport(
            prior_study_uid="A",
            current_study_uid="B",
            prior_quality_status=QualityStatus.OK,
            current_quality_status=QualityStatus.OK,
        )
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            report.status = ComparisonStatus.REVIEW  # type: ignore[misc]

    def test_defaults(self):
        report = ComparisonReport(
            prior_study_uid="A",
            current_study_uid="B",
            prior_quality_status=QualityStatus.OK,
            current_quality_status=QualityStatus.OK,
        )
        assert report.status == ComparisonStatus.STABLE
        assert report.reasons == []

def _metrics(
    mean_intensity: float = 128.0,
    std_intensity: float = 30.0,
    min_intensity: float = 10.0,
    max_intensity: float = 240.0,
    intensity_range: float = 230.0,
    foreground_fraction: float = 0.40,
) -> ImageQualityMetrics:
    return ImageQualityMetrics(
        mean_intensity=mean_intensity,
        std_intensity=std_intensity,
        min_intensity=min_intensity,
        max_intensity=max_intensity,
        intensity_range=intensity_range,
        foreground_fraction=foreground_fraction,
    )


def _seg(
    foreground_pixels: int = 26214,  # ~40% of 256x256
    foreground_fraction: float = 0.40,
    largest_contour_area: float = 25000.0,
    has_contours: bool = True,
) -> SegmentationQuality:
    return SegmentationQuality(
        foreground_pixels=foreground_pixels,
        foreground_fraction=foreground_fraction,
        largest_contour_area=largest_contour_area,
        has_contours=has_contours,
    )

    study_uid: str = "1.2.3",

    quality_status: QualityStatus = QualityStatus.OK,
    quality_flags: list = None,
    quality_metrics: ImageQualityMetrics = None,

) -> DecisionReport:
    return DecisionReport(
        study_uid=study_uid,
        series_uid=series_uid,
        plane=plane,
        num_slices=num_slices,
        image_height=256,
        image_width=256,
        quality_metrics=quality_metrics or _metrics(),

                         "outputs are not clinically validated and are not a diagnosis.")

IMAGE_PANEL_HEIGHT = 280  # display-only height (px) of each panel in the 2x2 image grid


def fit_panel_height(image, height=IMAGE_PANEL_HEIGHT, nearest=False):
    """Aspect-preserving copy scaled to `height` px for display only; the input array is never modified."""
    rows, cols = image.shape[:2]
    if rows == 0 or cols == 0:
        return image
    scale = height / rows
    if nearest:
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_NEAREST
    else:
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_AREA if scale < 1 else cv2.INTER_LINEAR
    return cv2.resize(np.ascontiguousarray(image), (max(1, round(cols * scale)), height), interpolation=interpolation)

def fit_panel_height(image, height=IMAGE_PANEL_HEIGHT, nearest=False):
    """Aspect-preserving copy scaled to `height` px for display only; the input array is never modified."""
    rows, cols = image.shape[:2]
    if rows == 0 or cols == 0:
        return image
    scale = height / rows
    if nearest:
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_NEAREST
    else:
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_AREA if scale < 1 else cv2.INTER_LINEAR
    return cv2.resize(np.ascontiguousarray(image), (max(1, round(cols * scale)), height), interpolation=interpolation)

                col3, col4 = st.columns(2)
                with col3:
                    panel = fit_panel_height(results["mask"], nearest=True)
                    st.markdown("##### Segmentation Mask")
                    st.image(panel, clamp=True, width=panel.shape[1])
                with col4:
                    overlay_rgb = results["overlay"][..., ::-1] if len(results["overlay"].shape) == 3 else results["overlay"]
                    panel = fit_panel_height(overlay_rgb)
                    st.markdown("##### Overlay")
                    st.image(panel, width=panel.shape[1])

            st.divider()
            st.subheader("Extracted Image Features")

            features = results["features"]
            formatted_features = {k: round(v, 2) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in features.items()}
            df = pd.DataFrame(list(formatted_features.items()), columns=["Feature", "Value"])
            st.dataframe(df, use_container_width=True)

            # Generate decision report if RSNA study
            if data_source == "Explore RSNA Studies" and study_metadata:
                st.divider()
                st.subheader("Quality Assessment Report")

                model_predictions = None

                # Inference logic: ensemble > smoke > production, in that priority order
                if use_ensemble_inference:
                    # Check if all 5 folds exist
                    all_folds_exist = all(p.is_file() for p in RSNA_ENSEMBLE_CHECKPOINT_PATHS)
                    if all_folds_exist:
                        try:
                            model_predictions = run_ensemble_inference(
                                metadata=metadata,
                                fold_checkpoint_paths=RSNA_ENSEMBLE_CHECKPOINT_PATHS,
                                study_uid=study_metadata["study_uid"],
                            )
                        except RSNAInferenceError as e:
                            st.warning(f"Ensemble inference unavailable for this study: {e}")
                    else:
                        missing_folds = [i for i, p in enumerate(RSNA_ENSEMBLE_CHECKPOINT_PATHS, start=1) if not p.is_file()]
                        st.info(f"5-fold ensemble not available (missing folds: {', '.join(map(str, missing_folds))}); "
                                "model predictions are unavailable.")
                else:
                    # Use existing smoke or production checkpoint
                    active_checkpoint_path = RSNA_SMOKE_CHECKPOINT_PATH if use_smoke_checkpoint else RSNA_CHECKPOINT_PATH
                    if active_checkpoint_path.is_file():
                        try:
                            model_predictions = run_inference(
                                metadata=metadata,
                                checkpoint_path=active_checkpoint_path,
                                study_uid=study_metadata["study_uid"],
                            )
                        except RSNAInferenceError as e:
                            st.warning(f"Model inference unavailable for this study: {e}")
                    elif use_smoke_checkpoint:
                        st.info(f"Smoke-test checkpoint not found at `{RSNA_SMOKE_CHECKPOINT_PATH.as_posix()}`; "
                                "model predictions are unavailable.")

                try:
                    decision_report = generate_decision_report(
                        study_uid=study_metadata["study_uid"],
                        series_uid=study_metadata["series_uid"],
                        plane=study_metadata["plane"],
                        volume_data=volume.raw_data,
                        preprocessed_data=results["preprocessed"],
                        mask=results["mask"],
                        features=features,
                        num_slices=study_metadata["num_slices"],
                        model_predictions=model_predictions,
                    )

                    # Display report summary
                    col_left, col_right = st.columns([1, 2])
                    with col_left:
                        status_color = {
                            "OK": "🟢",
                            "REVIEW": "🟡",
                            "INVALID": "🔴"
                        }
                        status_text = decision_report.quality_status.value
                        st.metric("Quality Status", f"{status_color[status_text]} {status_text}")

                    with col_right:
                        st.write("**Study Information**")
                        st.write(f"Study UID: `{decision_report.study_uid}`")
                        st.write(f"Plane: {decision_report.plane}")
                        st.write(f"Volume: {decision_report.num_slices} slices, {decision_report.image_height}×{decision_report.image_width}px")

                    # Quality metrics
                    st.write("**Image Quality Metrics**")
                    metrics_col1, metrics_col2, metrics_col3 = st.columns(3)
                    with metrics_col1:
                        st.metric("Mean Intensity", f"{decision_report.quality_metrics.mean_intensity:.1f}")
                        st.metric("Std Deviation", f"{decision_report.quality_metrics.std_intensity:.1f}")
                    with metrics_col2:
                        st.metric("Intensity Range", f"{decision_report.quality_metrics.intensity_range:.1f}")
                        st.metric("Foreground %", f"{decision_report.quality_metrics.foreground_fraction*100:.1f}%")
                    with metrics_col3:
                        st.metric("Foreground Pixels", f"{decision_report.segmentation_quality.foreground_pixels:,}")
                        st.metric("Contours Found", "Yes" if decision_report.segmentation_quality.has_contours else "No")

                    # Quality flags
                    if decision_report.quality_flags:
                        st.warning(f"**Quality Flags:** {'; '.join(decision_report.quality_flags)}")

                    # Model status
                    st.info(f"**Model Status:** {decision_report.model_status}")

                    if decision_report.model_predictions is not None:
                        if use_ensemble_inference:
                            st.warning(RSNA_ENSEMBLE_WARNING)

                            st.warning(RSNA_SMOKE_WARNING)

                        )

                        )
                        prior_decision_report = generate_decision_report(
                            study_uid=prior_study_metadata["study_uid"],
                            series_uid=prior_study_metadata["series_uid"],
                            plane=prior_study_metadata["plane"],
                            volume_data=prior_volume.raw_data,
                            preprocessed_data=prior_results["preprocessed"],
                            mask=prior_results["mask"],
                            features=prior_results["features"],
                            num_slices=prior_study_metadata["num_slices"],
                        )

                        # Side-by-side overlay images.
                        cg_col1, cg_col2 = st.columns(2)
                        with cg_col1:
                            st.markdown(f"**Prior study** — `{prior_study_metadata['study_uid']}`")
                            prior_overlay = prior_results["overlay"]
                            prior_overlay_rgb = (
                                prior_overlay[..., ::-1]
                                if len(prior_overlay.shape) == 3

                            )
                            st.image(

                            curr_overlay = results["overlay"]
                            curr_overlay_rgb = (

                                if len(curr_overlay.shape) == 3

                            st.image(
                                fit_panel_height(curr_overlay_rgb),
                                caption=f"Quality: {decision_report.quality_status.value}",
                            )

                        try:
                            comparison = generate_comparison_report(
                                prior=prior_decision_report,
                                current=decision_report,

                        except ValueError as cmp_err:
                            # INVALID quality blocks a meaningful comparison.
                            st.error(
                                f"ChangeGuard comparison cannot run: {cmp_err} "

                                status_label = "🟢 STABLE"
                                summary_sentence = (
                                    "No image-derived change candidates exceeded "
                                    "the configured review thresholds."
                                )
                            else:
                                card_bg   = "#fff3cd"
                                card_border = "#e0a800"
                                status_label = "🟡 REVIEW"
                                # Condense reason strings to their opening clause
                                # (everything before the first period or the full
                                # string if no period found).
                                short_reasons = []
                                for r in comparison.reasons:
                                    clause = r.split(".")[0].strip()
                                    short_reasons.append(clause)
                                summary_sentence = "; ".join(short_reasons) + "."

                            st.markdown(
                                f"""
<div style="
    background:{card_bg};
    border-left:5px solid {card_border};
    border-radius:6px;
    padding:1rem 1.25rem;
    margin-bottom:1rem;
">
  <p style="font-size:1.15rem;font-weight:700;margin:0 0 0.35rem 0;">

  </p>
